events.speaker: Riverhold Council
events.title: A promise we can keep
events.text:
Ironvale has a hundred like this. Pinewatch has the timber. We have the river between them.

And what do we have to offer?

A crossing. If they believe we'll finish it.

The hired ferry can take a small load now. Enough to learn the route, and prove we deliver. The High Pass closes with the snow. We should use the time we have.

Then we begin small. What can we send without risking the town's reserves?

I will put the quantity, the price, and the arrival date in front of you. We can choose a smaller shipment. The charter already gives you authority to trade within the public budget.

And while that cargo travels, I will inspect the foundations. There is work here worth saving.

Good. Show me the stores and the landing. We make the first promise when we know we can keep it.

events.speaker: Mira Holt
events.title: A promise kept
events.text:
That delivery is in the ledger. One kept promise gives our neighbours a reason to trade again.

Check what remains in Riverhold's stores before we offer the next cargo.
events.context: Show only after the first delivery actually arrives. Authored demo dialogue; no recorded clip supplied.

events.speaker: Mira Holt
events.title: An overdue promise
events.text:
The arrival date has passed. We owe our neighbours an honest account of what went wrong.

Read the terms in the ledger, keep the town fed, and inspect the route before making another promise. A failed agreement need not become a failed town.
events.context: Show only when a contract deadline is missed. Consequences and amounts come from the simulation; this dialogue grants no waiver or resources.

events.speaker: Ira Fen
events.title: Winter at the High Pass
events.text:
Snow is closing the High Pass to outside supplies. The routes below it still connect the valley, if we keep them working.

Count the reserves. Check the journey before you promise its arrival date. We still have neighbours, and we still have work to do.
events.context: Winter transition. Internal valley routes remain possible; this dialogue does not claim universal road closure or a forced famine.

events.speaker: Rowan Ash
events.title: Riverhold keeps its word
events.text:
We have given Riverhold a beginning worth keeping: work that feeds the town, a route our neighbours can use, and a promise carried through.

There will be harder seasons. For now, let the ledger show what our people made possible.
events.context: Show on the demo objective being met. A local milestone, not the end of the four-act campaign or a claim that all factions signed an accord.

events.speaker: Mira Holt
events.title: A smaller promise
events.text:
We can still put the accounts in order. Start with the food the town needs, then the inputs our workshops are missing.

Reduce commitments that outstrip the stores. Restore one useful connection and give one reliable delivery a chance. The next promise can be smaller.
events.context: Recoverable setback or continuation advice. No free cargo, accepted loan, automatic rescue or forgiven penalty is implied.

events.speaker: Rowan Ash
events.title: Riverhold stands again
events.text:
Winter did not have the last word. We have met the charter's terms and given Riverhold a footing again.

We took longer than we hoped. Let the ledger show that our people stayed, repaired what failed, and kept working until their neighbours could rely on them.
events.context: Show when the charter objectives are achieved after the winter deadline. This is a recovered outcome, distinct from the recovery advice event. Authored dialogue only.

events.speaker: Narrator
events.title: A crossing worth keeping
events.text:
Twelve years ago, the river gates failed. Fields drowned. Roads emptied. The River Crown fell, and the cities of the Veyran Basin learned to survive apart.

Some remember stolen grain. Some remember repair crews that never came. Every city keeps a different account of the Breaking.

Now winter gathers above the High Pass. At Riverhold, a damaged landing serves a working farm, a timber crew, and families who have decided to stay. Beneath their crossing, the old foundations still hold.

The council has chosen you as First Steward. There are warehouses to mend, neighbors to bargain with, and promises your people will have to live by.

Beyond the fields, forgotten gates hum beneath dry canals. Their secrets can wait. The first shipment cannot.

Begin with a road. A mill. A promise you can keep. The basin will learn your city's name.

events.speaker: Ira Fen
events.title: Ira: two river routes
events.text: I surveyed both channels this morning. The near bank gives us a shorter crossing, but the old landing can only unload one boat at a time. The deeper bend takes longer and has room for heavier cargo. Neither route improves because we wish it would. Choose what the shipment needs, leave room for the river to surprise us, and I will tell the crew where we are going.
